title: Vanishing of the left base-change term of the Jacobi-Zariski sequence
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings such that $H_1(L_{B/A})=0$ and the module of Kähler differentials $\Omega_{B/A}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] is a projective $B$-module, where $\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}=\bigl(N_1\xrightarrow{\ \delta\ }N_0\bigr)$, $N_1=I/I^2$, $N_0=\bigoplus_{b\in B}B\,\mathrm d[b]$, is the naive cotangent complex of the canonical presentation $A[B]\to B$ and $H_1(L_{B/A})=\ker\delta$, as in [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]. Let $\mathfrak a\subseteq B$ be an ideal and $C=B/\mathfrak a$, and let $\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}\otimes_BC$ be the two-term complex $N_1\otimes_BC\xrightarrow{\ \delta\otimes\mathrm{id}_C\ }N_0\otimes_BC$. Then $$H_1(\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}\otimes_BC)=\ker(\delta\otimes\mathrm{id}_C)\cong H_1(L_{B/A})\otimes_BC=0.$$ More precisely, the map $H_1(L_{B/A})\otimes_BC\to N_1\otimes_BC$ induced by the inclusion $\ker\delta\subseteq N_1$ is injective with image $\ker(\delta\otimes\mathrm{id}_C)$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00S2 (lemma-exact-sequence-NL), final assertion ('if Tor_1^B(Omega_{B/A},C) = Tor_2^B(Omega_{B/A},C) = 0 then H_1(NL_{B/A} (x)_B C) = H_1(L_{B/A}) (x)_B C') and its proof, lines 35444-35446 and 35467-35485; here the Tor hypotheses are replaced by projectivity of Omega_{B/A}, which implies them

proof.text: For the canonical presentation P, H_1(L_{B/A}) is the kernel of the conormal differential delta. The zero-H_1 hypothesis therefore makes delta injective (Mathlib Algebra.Extension.subsingleton_h1Cotangent). The sequence N_1 -> N_0 -> Omega_{B/A} -> 0 is exact and its last arrow is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-naive-cotangent-complex-cokernel-kahler]. Consequently 0 -> N_1 -> N_0 -> Omega_{B/A} -> 0 is a short exact sequence.

Projectivity of Omega_{B/A} gives its flatness by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-module-flat]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-quotient-tensor-injective] directly to the short exact sequence in the preceding step and the module C = B/a. It follows that id_C tensor delta is injective. Tensor symmetry (Mathlib LinearMap.lTensor_inj_iff_rTensor_inj) gives injectivity of delta tensor id_C. Its kernel is therefore zero. Because H_1 was already zero, there is no need to factor delta through its image, to prove that image flat, or to use freeness of N_0.

The tensor H_1(L_{B/A}) tensor_B C is a zero module (Mathlib TensorProduct.uniqueLeft). The tensored kernel inclusion has subsingleton source, hence is injective and is the zero map; its image is the zero submodule, equal to the kernel of the tensored differential by the preceding step. The latter kernel is also subsingleton. Mathlib LinearEquiv.ofSubsingleton supplies the linear equivalence between these two zero modules, establishing every conjunct in the conclusion.
